sections.h2: What should a Lexington homeowner know before selling fast?
sections.html:
Lexington is a city and a county in one: the city limits match Fayette County, and the two governments have been merged since 1974. The Census Bureau counted 322,570 people in 2020 and estimated 329,751 on July 1, 2025. Its 2020-2024 figures show 139,715 households, a median owner-occupied value of $293,500 and an owner-occupied rate of 53.8 percent.

That last number matters to a seller. Nearly half of Lexington households rent, so a house here often has a landlord, an investor or a student renter on the other side of the deal. A buyer who can close without a lender's appraisal and repair demands gives you a faster path when the house is tired, tenant-occupied or tied up in an estate.

sections.h2: How does Lexington's urban service area affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Lexington drew a line around itself early. In 1958 the city adopted an urban service area, described as the first urban growth boundary in the country, and kept a 40-acre minimum for land outside it so the horse farms stayed whole. The line was widened by 5,300 acres in 1996, which is why newer subdivisions sit on the edge of a city that is still about 285 square miles in total.

Land outside the boundary follows different zoning rules from land inside it. If your house is near the edge, ask the Division of Planning which side of the line it sits on before you set a price or accept an offer.

  • The University of Kentucky is the largest employer, with 16,743 employees in 2020.
  • Fayette County Public Schools employs 5,374 people, and the area's four main hospitals employ about 7,000 together.
  • Toyota's Kentucky plant is in neighboring Georgetown, within the Lexington combined statistical area.
  • Interstate 75 runs along the edge of the city and Interstate 64 along its northern side.

Fayette County Public Schools runs six district high schools, 12 middle schools and 37 elementary schools. Summers are hot and humid and winters moderately cold, in the USDA 6b zone, so roofs, gutters and HVAC age on an ordinary schedule and inspectors tend to look at them first.

sections.h2: Who lives in Lexington, and who is likely to buy your house?
sections.html:
Lexington is a college town with a professional workforce. The 2020-2024 Census figures show that 48.3 percent of residents aged 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree, median household income is $69,479, and per capita income is $43,790. About 11.9 percent of residents were born abroad, and roughly 196 languages are spoken across the city, with Spanish and Swahili the most common after English.

The same data shows that 79.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so about one in five had moved in the prior year. Buyers include University of Kentucky staff, hospital workers, horse industry employees who work around Keeneland and the Kentucky Horse Park, and investors who rent to students. Transylvania University and Bluegrass Community and Technical College add to the rental demand.

Lexington's government is a nonpartisan mayor-council with 12 council districts and three members elected at large. Zoning, permits and rental licenses all run through the urban county government, and the Lexington-Fayette metro area of 516,811 people also takes in Clark, Jessamine, Bourbon, Woodford and Scott counties, so many buyers arrive from those neighbors.

sections.h2: What rules apply if your Lexington house has been a short-term rental?
sections.html:
A house used for stays under 30 days must hold a special fees license from the Division of Revenue, and running one without it can draw fines of up to $500 a day. If you are selling a property that was listed on a booking site, gather the license, the Zoning Compliance Permit and the insurance certificate, because a buyer will ask for them.

The application also asks for a site plan showing legal off-street parking, a sworn safety affidavit and, for septic properties, proof the tank fits the stated occupancy. Hosted rentals need two documents showing a permanent resident lives on site. A cash buyer can take the house with the license history unresolved, but you should tell them what you know.

sections.h2: How do Kentucky's transfer tax and recording work on a Lexington sale?
sections.html:
Kentucky puts its real estate transfer tax on the seller. KRS 142.050 sets it at fifty cents for each $500 of value declared in the deed, and the Fayette County Clerk collects it before the deed is accepted for recording. At the median owner-occupied value of $293,500 that is $293.50, and a $350,000 sale produces $350.

  • The tax is collected once per transaction, in the county where the deed must be recorded.
  • Transfers in foreclosure or by deed in lieu of foreclosure, and transfers between spouses in a divorce, are exempt.
  • The Fayette County Clerk also records mortgages and releases, so any lien on the property has to be released of record before or at closing.

The clerk's office prepares the county's property tax bills as well, so the same counter can answer questions about the deed, the bill mailing address and the lien releases.

sections.h2: What happens to the Fayette County property tax bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
Fayette County values property as of January 1 and bills on the rates set by the urban county government, Fayette County Schools, the state and other taxing districts. The Fayette County PVA says bills are due by December 31 and that penalties for paying late are substantial.

The bill is issued in the name of the January 1 owner. If the house sold after that date, the bill goes in care of the new owner, though a sale close to printing time may not be updated in time. Prorating the year between you and the buyer is a closing-table job, so ask the closing agent or attorney how the split will be calculated.

Owners who are 65 or older, or who receive disability payments, may qualify for the Homestead Exemption through the PVA. If you think the 2026 assessment is wrong, the PVA accepts review requests, though the finalized assessment does not change for the current bill.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Lexington house?
sections.html:
A cash offer fits best when time or condition is the main problem. It is less useful when your house is move-in ready and you can wait through showings.

  • An inherited house in a Fayette County estate where the heirs live elsewhere.
  • A rental with tenants, deferred repairs or an expired short-term rental license.
  • A house behind on mortgage payments, where a quick closing can stop further fees.
  • A property needing work that an appraiser or lender would flag.

With a cash sale you skip listing prep and lender timelines, but you still owe the transfer tax and any payoff. Ask for the offer in writing, compare it with what a listing would net after repairs and carrying costs, and decide from the numbers.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Lexington house sale?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for every $500 of value in the deed, paid by the seller. A $293,500 sale, the Census median owner-occupied value for Lexington, comes to $293.50, collected by the Fayette County Clerk when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Who pays the Lexington property tax bill if I sell in the fall?
faqs.a: The bill is issued to the January 1 owner, and the PVA says it is due by December 31. If you sell during the year, the closing agent normally prorates it between you and the buyer, so confirm that with them before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to sell a Lexington house that was an Airbnb?
faqs.a: No license is needed to sell, but an unlicensed rental can draw fines of up to $500 a day, so close the licensing question out first. Gather the Zoning Compliance Permit, business license and special fees license records if you have them.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lexington house with tenants still living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. About 46 percent of Lexington households rent, so buyers who take tenanted houses are common. Give the buyer the lease and deposit details, and ask your closing agent how the deposit transfers.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after a Lexington sale?
faqs.a: At the Fayette County Clerk, which handles land records for the whole county. The clerk computes the transfer tax, collects it and certifies the payment on the deed before recording.
